## Auditable
*path:* Transparent

- **The ENCODE Uniform Analysis Pipelines** _(medium)_
  The team built their data-processing system so that every result file carries a complete, traceable record of where it came from — the exact raw data, the specific software versions, and the parameters used to produce it — with all the code posted publicly and quality 'audit badges' flagging questionable results. It's a concrete look at making an entire analysis pipeline traceable end-to-end.
  https://doi.org/10.1101/2023.04.04.535623
- **A multi-omics data analysis workflow packaged as a FAIR Digital Object** _(medium)_
  To make their own analysis traceable, the team published every step of their data-processing pipeline as version-controlled, openly available code, wrapped each step in a self-contained software container so anyone can re-run it, and attached rich machine-readable records of what each step does plus a stand-in dataset that mimics the real (privacy-protected) data — a worked example of a study someone else could inspect and reproduce end to end.
  https://doi.org/10.1093/gigascience/giad115
- **How tool combinations in different pipeline versions affect the outcome in RNA-seq analysis** _(high)_
  Every step is laid out so a stranger could retrace it: exact version numbers for every tool used, the full run commands listed in a supplement, public accession IDs for all three datasets, and the analysis code plus data deposited in an open archive — a concrete look at making a complex analysis fully checkable by others.
  https://doi.org/10.1093/nargab/lqae020

## Documented
*path:* Careful › Meticulous

- **Study Protocol for the Fukushima Health Management Survey** _(medium)_
  This published protocol spells out the entire survey apparatus in exhaustive detail — exact equipment specifications (probe frequency, image-saving requirements), the precise qualifications examiners must hold, the numeric thresholds that sort each thyroid result into categories, age-by-age lists of every measurement taken, and the calendar for each round of follow-up. A concrete look at writing down a study's machinery so completely that another team could rebuild it.
  https://doi.org/10.2188/jea.je20120105
- **A Comprehensive Report on Ultrasonic Attenuation of Engineering Materials, Including Metals, Ceramics, Polymers, Fiber-Reinforced Composites, Wood, and Rocks** _(medium)_
  The team ran 336 separate measurements across metals, ceramics, polymers, composites, wood, and rocks, and laid every result out in tables along with the two methods they first checked for reliability — a concrete example of recording a large body of measurements so fully that others can reuse them.
  https://doi.org/10.3390/app10072230
- **The stepped wedge trial design: a systematic review** _(medium)_
  To make their review repeatable, the authors spelled out every search phrase and database they queried, the exact months they ran the searches, their inclusion and exclusion rules, and even attached the blank form they used to pull the same set of facts from each study they examined.
  https://doi.org/10.1186/1471-2288-6-54

## Pre-registered
*path:* Rigorous › Warranted

- **Measuring the crowd within again: a pre-registered replication study** _(high)_
  Before collecting any data, the researchers publicly lodged their full plan — sample sizes, data-exclusion rules, and exact analyses — on an open registry, then clearly flagged which findings followed that plan and which were exploratory afterthoughts. A concrete look at how locking in your method in advance keeps a result from being shaped by the data.
  https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2014.00786
- **A study protocol to investigate the management of depression and challenging behaviors associated with dementia in aged care settings** _(medium)_
  Before collecting any data, the authors laid out their plan in public — registering the trial and publishing this full protocol with its specific predictions, group assignments, measures, and planned statistics all stated in advance. It's a concrete look at committing to a study design upfront so results can't be quietly reshaped later.
  https://doi.org/10.1186/1471-2318-13-95
- **Protocol for an HIV Pre-exposure Prophylaxis (PrEP) Population Level Intervention Study in Victoria Australia: The PrEPX Study** _(high)_
  This is the study's full plan — its aims, hypotheses, who's eligible, the target sample size and how it was justified, and the exact statistical tests — all published before any results, and the trial was logged in advance in a public registry with a citable number. A clear example of committing to your method up front.
  https://doi.org/10.3389/fpubh.2018.00151

## Consistent
*path:* Rigorous › Warranted

- **Sensitivity analysis in multiple imputation in effectiveness studies of psychotherapy** _(medium)_
  The team re-ran their entire analysis under a deliberately pessimistic alternative assumption about why patients dropped out, and found their conclusions barely shifted — the same predictors held up. It's a concrete look at showing a finding doesn't hinge on a debatable assumption.
  https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2015.01042
- **Multicriteria Approach towards the Sustainable Selection of a Teahouse Location with Sensitivity Analysis** _(medium)_
  To make sure their chosen location wasn't an artifact of one calculation method, the researchers ran the same decision problem through two independent ranking techniques and a randomized stress-test of the criteria weights, checking that the winning answer held up across all of them.
  https://doi.org/10.3390/su10082926
- **Hadronic uncertainties in B → K ∗ μ + μ −: a state-of-the-art analysis** _(medium)_
  To trust their own conclusion, the authors re-did the calculation using two completely different sets of underlying inputs and two different theoretical methods, and showed the answers agreed closely; they also reproduced an earlier numerical result with a clean hand-derived formula — treating that convergence as the evidence their result holds.
  https://doi.org/10.1007/jhep04(2017)016

**Considered but not accepted:**
- A Hybrid MCDM Technique for Risk Management in Construction Projects — This is a method-development paper proposing a decision-making technique (with an illustrative example), not a substantive study whose conclusion is warranted by consistency; the word 'consistent' is just a borrowed method label. — https://doi.org/10.3390/sym10020046

## Impartial
*path:* Fair

- **Exercise for osteoarthritis of the knee** _(medium)_
  Every study was screened, its data pulled out, and its risk of bias judged by two reviewers working separately, with a third reviewer brought in to settle any disagreement — a built-in guard so no single person's leaning could tilt what got included or how it was scored.

- **Ketone monoester increases circulating levels of <scp>LEAP2</scp> and decreases appetite in healthy men** _(medium)_
  To keep their comparison from being skewed by what participants could taste or expect, the researchers made the comparison drinks identical in volume and calories and even doctored the plain-water placebo with a bitter additive and sweetener so it tasted like the real drink — then served all three in random, blinded order.

## Reflexive
*path:* Humble

- **Bi5: An Autoethnographic Analysis of a Lived Experience Suicide Attempt Survivor Through Grief Concepts and ‘Participant’ Positionality in Community Research** _(high)_
  The author turns the analytic lens on themselves, writing out how their own identity and life history—as a suicide-attempt survivor, a racialized Muslim, genderfluid, with a bipolar diagnosis—shape what they can see in the research, and includes a frank statement examining their own position as both subject and investigator.
  https://doi.org/10.3390/socsci14070405
- **Barriers and facilitators to culturally sensitive care in general practice: a reflexive thematic analysis** _(medium)_
  The authors explicitly treated their findings as something they constructed rather than objectively uncovered — stating that the themes were 'generated rather than revealed' — and they reflected on how their own mixed backgrounds (sociologists, an anthropologist, a doctor) and the back-and-forth between coders shaped the interpretation. A concrete look at researchers owning their hand in making the result.
  https://doi.org/10.1186/s12875-024-02630-y
- **Neurosurgeons’ experiences of conducting and disseminating clinical research in low-income and middle-income countries: a reflexive thematic analysis** _(high)_
  The researchers turned the analytic lens on themselves: they kept a reflexive diary throughout, named the interviewer's own identity (a white British nurse-researcher from a high-income country interviewing surgeons in poorer countries) and openly stated that their findings are shaped by that lens, even recommending future work be led by people from within those countries instead.
  https://doi.org/10.1136/bmjopen-2021-051806

- It’s personal: navigating research questions that stem from our lived experiences — This is a commentary that discusses and advocates for reflexivity and positionality as a practice; reflexivity is its subject matter, not the method of a substantive study that enacted it to warrant a finding. — https://doi.org/10.1093/ije/dyae132

## Generalizable
*path:* Reliable › Robust

- **Enhanced motor noise in an autism subtype with poor motor skills** _(high)_
  Before trusting their two-group split, the researchers held back part of their data, found the groupings on the rest, then checked whether the same groupings reappeared in the untouched portion — they report it held up 89% of the time, a concrete demonstration of testing whether a finding carries over to fresh cases.
  https://doi.org/10.1186/s13229-024-00618-0
- **Helmets for preventing injury in motorcycle riders** _(medium)_
  By pooling 61 studies done in many different countries, with different designs and over different decades, the authors show the same protective effect turns up again and again — and they formally test that the studies don't disagree — making the case that the finding holds well beyond any single setting.
  https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.cd004333.pub3
- **Generalization of Cortical MOSTest Genome-Wide Associations Within and Across Samples** _(medium)_
  The researchers checked whether the genetic signals they found in one large group held up in a completely separate group of people who were, on average, 50 years younger — showing the findings carry over across independent samples and very different ages.
  https://doi.org/10.1101/2021.04.23.441215

- **Multi-centre deep learning for placenta segmentation in obstetric ultrasound with multi-observer and cross-country generalization** _(high)_
  After building their placenta-finding tool on images from Denmark, the team retested it unchanged on a separate set of images collected in another country (Spain) and showed it still performed at a similar level — a concrete demonstration that the result holds beyond the population it was built on.

## Structured
*path:* Clear

- **Potential Causes of Titanium Particle and Ion Release in Implant Dentistry: A Systematic Review** _(medium)_
  Before searching, the authors cast their questions into a fixed template — who is studied, what is done to them, against what comparison, and what outcome is measured — and then followed a published checklist for deciding which studies to keep; a concrete look at organizing a review by an explicit skeleton rather than ad hoc.
  https://doi.org/10.3390/ijms19113585
- **Body Awareness: Construct and Self-Report Measures** _(medium)_
  To compare a dozen existing questionnaires fairly, the team ran each through the same fixed evaluation checklist, then sorted the questions they contained into an explicit framework of four domains and eleven sub-domains — a concrete example of imposing an orderly scaffold on a messy body of material.
  https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0005614
- **Use of relative and absolute effect measures in reporting health inequalities: structured review** _(medium)_
  To survey how health studies report differences between groups, the authors set up a fixed, repeatable plan in advance — a defined set of ten journals, one publication year, and a small list of exactly what to count in each article — then tallied every paper against those same categories, so the whole review runs on an explicit scaffold rather than impressions.
  https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.e5774

## Caveated
*path:* Honest › Candid

- **The International Glossary on Infertility and Fertility Care, 2017** _(medium)_
  Rather than presenting their agreed-upon terminology as final, the authors openly flag its boundaries: they note the definitions rest on expert consensus rather than empirical testing, and that some terms will need future revision as science and society change. Many individual definitions also carry their own caveats (e.g. that reference criteria or denominators must be specified when results are reported).
  https://doi.org/10.1016/j.fertnstert.2017.06.005
- **ChatGPT applications in medical, dental, pharmacy, and public health education: A descriptive study highlighting the advantages and limitations** _(medium)_
  The authors close by flagging three concrete limits on their own conclusions: only a handful of evaluators made subjective judgments, the strict word-count instruction they imposed may have cut out relevant information, and whole disciplines (nursing, medical technology) were left untested — so readers know exactly how far to trust the findings.
  https://doi.org/10.52225/narra.v3i1.103
- **Cognitive training with casual video games: points to consider** _(high)_
  Throughout, the authors flag the limits of their own findings rather than overselling them: they note that lab staff knew who was in which group, that a survey instruction error forced them to drop some data, that one questionnaire result 'must be taken lightly' because of a tiny sample, and they close by saying more research is needed before claiming real-world benefit. A concrete look at a study hedging its own conclusions.
  https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2013.01010

  Rather than picking studies that fit a conclusion, the team searched eight databases, screened all 4,463 hits against pre-set eligibility rules, and reported the full spread of results — including correlations ranging from strongly negative to strongly positive and the inconvenient finding that self-reports were sometimes higher, sometimes lower than direct measures.

## Blinded
*path:* Honest › Disinterested

- **Comparison of Crocus sativus L. and imipramine in the treatment of mild to moderate depression: A pilot double-blind randomized trial [ISRCTN45683816]** _(high)_
  To keep judgments unbiased, the researchers disguised the two treatments as identical red capsules matched in color, size, form, and taste, and kept the patients, the doctor giving the medication, and the symptom-rater all unaware of who got which — a concrete example of how blinding is built into a trial.
  https://doi.org/10.1186/1472-6882-4-12
- **Effect of Probiotic Supplementation on Cognitive Function and Metabolic Status in Alzheimer's Disease: A Randomized, Double-Blind and Controlled Trial** _(high)_
  Neither the patients nor the researchers knew who was drinking the real probiotic milk versus plain milk; the random assignment was sealed and kept hidden until all the analyses were finished, so no one's expectations could tilt the cognitive scoring or the lab measurements.
  https://doi.org/10.3389/fnagi.2016.00256
- **Lactobacillus johnsonii N6.2 Modulates the Host Immune Responses: A Double-Blind, Randomized Trial in Healthy Adults** _(high)_
  The study was run so neither participants nor the staff interacting with them knew who got the live bacteria versus a placebo: the probiotic and the inert skim-milk capsules were made identical, bottled under treatment codes by a separate collaborator who never met the participants — a concrete look at how a trial removes the experimenters' own expectations from the result.
  https://doi.org/10.3389/fimmu.2017.00655

## Blinded
*path:* Rigorous › Controlled

- **Effect of Probiotic Supplementation on Cognitive Function and Metabolic Status in Alzheimer's Disease: A Randomized, Double-Blind and Controlled Trial** _(high)_
  To compare probiotics against plain milk, the team kept both patients and the researchers in the dark about who got which drink — the allocation was concealed until all analyses were done — so expectations couldn't tilt how outcomes like the memory test were scored.

## Concealed
*path:* Rigorous › Controlled › Randomized

- **Multi-System Physical Exercise Intervention for Fall Prevention and Quality of Life in Pre-Frail Older Adults: A Randomized Controlled Trial** _(medium)_
  When assigning each older adult to the exercise or comparison group, the team kept the upcoming assignment hidden from whoever was enrolling people, so no one could steer who landed in which group — a real example of guarding the draw from being gamed.
  https://doi.org/10.3390/ijerph17093102
- **Integrated versus nonintegrated peripheral intravenous catheter in hospitalized adults (OPTIMUM): A randomized controlled trial** _(high)_
  Group assignments were generated centrally by a web-based service and revealed only at the moment a patient entered the study, so the staff enrolling and inserting catheters could not foresee or steer which patient got which device — a clean example of keeping the upcoming assignment hidden until commitment.
  https://doi.org/10.1002/jhm.12995
- **CT coronary angiography in patients with suspected angina due to coronary heart disease (SCOT-HEART): an open-label, parallel-group, multicentre trial** _(high)_
  To assign each patient to a group, the team used a web-based system specifically so that whoever was enrolling a patient could not know or influence which group that patient would land in until the moment of assignment — a clean example of keeping the upcoming assignment hidden.
  https://doi.org/10.1016/s0140-6736(15)60291-4

**Considered but not accepted:**
- Association Between Risk-of-Bias Assessments and Results of Randomized Trials in Cochrane Reviews: The ROBES Meta-Epidemiologic Study — This meta-epidemiological study studies allocation concealment as its subject matter—measuring how concealment judgements relate to trial results—rather than itself being a randomized trial that concealed its allocation. — https://doi.org/10.1093/aje/kwx344
- Design, analysis, and presentation of crossover trials — This is a methodological review that counts how often crossover trials reported allocation concealment; it studies concealment rather than being a concealed randomized trial itself. — https://doi.org/10.1186/1745-6215-10-27
- The quality of reports of randomised trials in 2000 and 2006: comparative study of articles indexed in PubMed — This is a survey measuring how often trials report allocation concealment; it studies the quality rather than being a trial that concealed its own allocation. — https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.c723
- The Effectiveness of Mobile-Health Technologies to Improve Health Care Service Delivery Processes: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis — This is a systematic review that assesses allocation concealment in other trials; it does not itself randomize participants with concealed allocation, so it discusses the quality rather than practicing it. — https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pmed.1001363
- Rehabilitation following carpal tunnel release — This is a systematic review that assessed whether other trials concealed their allocation; it is not itself a randomized trial that practiced allocation concealment, so it studies the quality rather than enacting it. — https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.cd004158.pub3
- Randomization Technique, Allocation Concealment, Masking, And Susceptibility Of Trials To Selection Bias — This paper analyzes and discusses allocation concealment as its subject matter, recommending how it should be reported, rather than being a trial that itself used concealed allocation. — https://doi.org/10.22237/jmasm/1051747680
- The unpredictability paradox: review of empirical comparisons of randomised and non-randomised clinical trials — This is a systematic review that studies the effect of allocation concealment in other trials rather than being a trial that itself concealed its random allocation. — https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.317.7167.1185
- The Need for Randomization in Animal Trials: An Overview of Systematic Reviews — This is a meta-review studying whether allocation concealment reduces bias in others' animal trials; it makes concealment its object of study rather than practicing concealment in its own design. — https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0098856
- Randomisation to protect against selection bias in healthcare trials — This is a meta-research review STUDYING the effects of allocation concealment, not a trial that itself was concealed. — https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.mr000012.pub3
- African HIV/AIDS Trials Are More Likely to Report Adequate Allocation Concealment and Random Generation than North American Trials — This is a meta-study that assesses allocation concealment in other trials rather than being a randomized trial that itself concealed allocation. — https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0003491
- What is the influence of randomisation sequence generation and allocation concealment on treatment effects of physical therapy trials? A meta-epidemiological study — This meta-epidemiological study STUDIES allocation concealment as its subject matter, measuring its effect on treatment estimates across trials, rather than itself being a concealed randomized trial. — https://doi.org/10.1136/bmjopen-2015-008562

## Falsifiable
*path:* Rigorous › Warranted

- **Normalization of Blood Pressure With Spinal Cord Epidural Stimulation After Severe Spinal Cord Injury** _(medium)_
  The researchers stated a specific, refutable prediction — that their spinal stimulation would lift chronically low blood pressure into a named target range — and exposed it to failure: they show stimulation settings that did NOT raise pressure alongside the ones that did, so the claim could plainly have come out false.
  https://doi.org/10.3389/fnhum.2018.00083
- **The Prosodic Acquisition Path Hypothesis: Towards explaining variability in L2 acquisition of phonology** _(medium)_
  The authors built their proposal to make narrow, refutable predictions about the exact order of difficulty learners face, then ran an experiment with English speakers learning Turkish whose results could have contradicted those predictions — a concrete case of staking a claim that could be proven wrong and testing it.
  https://doi.org/10.5334/gjgl.47
- **Severe Periodontitis and Risk for Poor Glycemic Control in Patients with Non‐Insulin‐Dependent Diabetes Mellitus** _(medium)_
  The researchers stated one clear prediction up front — that severe gum disease would worsen blood-sugar control — and pinned it to exact, measurable cut-offs (specific bone/gum-loss levels, a specific blood-sugar threshold) defined before looking at outcomes, so the data could plainly have come back showing no link and refuted them.
  http://hdl.handle.net/2027.42/141809

- Foundational Requirements for Artificial General Intelligence: A Falsifiable Framework Based on Signal Prediction — The paper proposes and argues for a 'falsifiable' benchmark as its subject matter rather than enacting falsifiability in testing its own substantive empirical claim; it discusses the quality, not practices it. — http://arxiv.org/abs/2504.04430

- From mechanism to phenotype: What fits in a basket trial — This is a commentary discussing trial design, sample size, and statistical power for basket trials rather than an empirical study that justified its own sample size with a power calculation. — https://doi.org/10.1002/epi.70086
- Applied Psychometrics: Sample Size and Sample Power Considerations in Factor Analysis (EFA, CFA) and SEM in General — This paper reviews sample-size and power rules for factor analysis—power is its subject matter, not a property of its own study. — https://doi.org/10.4236/psych.2018.98126
- Using Effect Size—or Why the P Value Is Not Enough — This is an instructional/methods article that teaches about effect size and statistical power; it studies and explains the quality rather than being a powered substantive study itself. — https://doi.org/10.4300/jgme-d-12-00156.1
- Sample Size Justification — This is an overview article that discusses and provides guidelines for sample size justification methods; it studies the quality rather than being a substantive study that was itself powered. — https://doi.org/10.1525/collabra.33267
- Statistical design and analysis for a 'biological effects' study — This paper discusses and recommends statistical design including sample-size formulae; it studies/characterizes the quality rather than being a substantive study that justified its own sample size. — https://doi.org/10.3354/meps046213
- Sample Size and Statistical Power Calculation in Genetic Association Studies — This paper studies and computes statistical power to produce sample-size guidelines; power is its subject matter, not a property of its own substantive inference. — https://doi.org/10.5808/gi.2012.10.2.117
- Description and Power Analysis of Two Tests for Detecting Recent Population Bottlenecks From Allele Frequency Data — The paper studies and characterizes the statistical power of two tests via simulation and produces sample-size guidelines — power is its subject matter, not a property warranting its own substantive inference. — https://doi.org/10.1093/genetics/144.4.2001
- Sample Size Determination and Statistical Power Analysis in PLS Using R: An Annotated Tutorial — This is a tutorial teaching how to conduct power analysis and sample-size determination; its subject matter is the quality itself rather than a substantive study that was powered. — https://doi.org/10.17705/1cais.03603
- The statistical analysis of mitochondrial DNA polymorphisms: chi 2 and the problem of small samples. — The paper develops a statistical method addressing power/small-sample issues; power is the object of study, not a property of an enacted substantive study. — https://doi.org/10.1093/oxfordjournals.molbev.a040568
- Sample Size Requirements for Discrete-Choice Experiments in Healthcare: a Practical Guide — This paper studies sample size/power requirements and produces a practical guide; it characterizes the quality rather than being a study that was itself powered. — https://doi.org/10.1007/s40271-015-0118-z
- Power and sample-size estimation for microbiome studies using pairwise distances and PERMANOVA — This paper develops a method and software for estimating power and sample size; it studies power rather than being a study that was itself powered. — https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btv183
- A solution to minimum sample size for regressions — The paper studies minimum sample size and statistical power as its subject matter, producing sample-size guidelines, rather than being a study that was itself adequately powered. — https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0229345
- Power analysis and sample size estimation for RNA-Seq differential expression — The paper simulates and characterizes statistical power and produces a sample-size tool — it studies power as its subject matter rather than being a study that was itself powered. — https://doi.org/10.1261/rna.046011.114
- Sample Size Guideline for Correlation Analysis — This paper studies and produces sample-size/power guidelines for correlation analysis; power is its subject matter, not a property of its own substantive inference. — https://doi.org/10.22158/wjssr.v3n1p37
- Sample size and power considerations in network meta-analysis — The paper develops methods for estimating effective sample size and statistical power in network meta-analysis — power is the object of study, not a property of the study itself. — https://doi.org/10.1186/2046-4053-1-41
- Simulation-Based Power Analysis for Factorial Analysis of Variance Designs — This is a methods/software tutorial that builds tools to compute statistical power; it studies and enables power analysis rather than being a substantive study that was itself adequately powered. — https://doi.org/10.1177/2515245920951503
- Trial Sequential Analysis in systematic reviews with meta-analysis — This paper develops and explains a methodology about required information size and controlling errors; statistical power is its subject matter, not a property of its own substantive inference. — https://doi.org/10.1186/s12874-017-0315-7
- Small sample sizes reduce the replicability of task-based fMRI studies — The paper studies and characterizes how sample size affects replicability rather than being a substantive study that justified its own sample size with a power calculation. — https://doi.org/10.1038/s42003-018-0073-z
- Statistical Practices of Educational Researchers: An Analysis of their ANOVA, MANOVA, and ANCOVA Analyses — This paper surveys whether other researchers based sample sizes on power considerations; it studies the practice of power analysis rather than being a powered study itself. — http://hdl.handle.net/10315/34607
- Sample Size Justification — This is an overview article that discusses and provides guidelines for justifying sample sizes; it studies the quality rather than being a study that was itself powered. — https://doi.org/10.31234/osf.io/9d3yf
- Statistical Analyses Support Power Law Distributions Found in Neuronal Avalanches — The paper concerns power-law distributions in neural activity, not statistical power; it never justifies its own sample size with a power analysis. — https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0019779
- Sample size determination for mediation analysis of longitudinal data — The paper studies and produces sample-size/power guidelines via simulation; power is its subject matter, not a property of its own substantive inference. — https://doi.org/10.1186/s12874-018-0473-2
- Power and sample size calculations for Mendelian randomization studies using one genetic instrument — This paper develops formulas FOR calculating power and sample size — power is its subject matter, not a property of its own substantive study. — https://doi.org/10.1093/ije/dyt110
- Reliability and Statistical Power: How Measurement Fallibility Affects Power and Required Sample Sizes for Several Parametric and Nonparametric Statistics — This paper studies statistical power itself via simulations to produce power and sample-size tables; power is the object of study, not a property warranting its own substantive inference. — https://doi.org/10.22237/jmasm/1177992480
- Effect Size Guidelines, Sample Size Calculations, and Statistical Power in Gerontology — The paper's subject matter is effect sizes and power itself—it produces sample-size guidelines rather than being a substantive study whose own conclusion was warranted by an a-priori power calculation. — https://doi.org/10.1093/geroni/igz036
- Sample Size Calculation: Inaccurate A Priori Assumptions for Nuisance Parameters Can Greatly Affect the Power of a Randomized Controlled Trial — This is a simulation study that characterizes how power is affected by inaccurate assumptions; power is its subject matter, not a property of its own substantive inference. — https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0132578
- Sample Size Calculations in Clinical Research — This is a letter arguing against a priori sample size calculations; it discusses/critiques the practice rather than being a powered study itself. — https://doi.org/10.1097/00000542-200210000-00050
- An interactive power analysis tool for microarray hypothesis testing and generation — The paper builds a power-analysis tool and studies how power varies by algorithm and organism — power is the object of study, not a property warranting its own substantive inference. — https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btk052
- A priori power considerations in orthodontic research: a 3 year meta-epidemiologic study — The paper studies the prevalence of power calculations in others' work rather than justifying its own sample size with a power analysis. — https://doi.org/10.1093/ejo/cjz061
- Does Raising Type 1 Error Rate Improve Power to Detect Interactions in Linear Regression Models? A Simulation Study — This is a simulation study that characterizes statistical power itself; power is the object of study, not a property warranting its own substantive inference. — https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0071079

## Systematic
*path:* Careful › Thorough

- **Blockchain Technology in Healthcare: A Systematic Review** _(high)_
  To survey blockchain in healthcare, the authors followed a published step-by-step review recipe (PRISMA), writing out a search protocol in advance and applying it identically across four databases to find, pull, and analyze every relevant study — a concrete look at a reproducible, rule-governed search.
  https://doi.org/10.3390/healthcare7020056
- **Mental Health of Children and Adolescents Amidst COVID-19 and Past Pandemics: A Rapid Systematic Review** _(high)_
  To survey what's known about children's mental health in pandemics, the authors followed a published step-by-step search-and-screen protocol: they pulled 5,828 articles, applied fixed inclusion rules, and narrowed to the 18 that qualified — a concrete look at running a search by an explicit, repeatable procedure rather than ad hoc picking.
  https://doi.org/10.3390/ijerph18073432
- **What do we know about community-based health worker programs? A systematic review of existing reviews on community health workers** _(high)_
  To map what is known about community health worker programs, the team searched eleven databases with peer-reviewed search strategies, screened over 4,000 records with two independent reviewers and a third to break ties, extracted data with a pilot-tested form, and rated each included review against a standard quality checklist — a concrete look at how an exhaustive, rule-governed evidence search is run.
  https://doi.org/10.1186/s12960-018-0304-x

## Systematic
*path:* Rigorous

- **A systematic review of the incidence of schizophrenia: the distribution of rates and the influence of sex, urbanicity, migrant status and methodology** _(high)_
  To find every study on the topic, the team searched four databases, hand-checked reference lists, presented conference posters, and wrote to study authors asking what they'd missed — then ran the collected studies through an explicit, pre-stated sequence of filters with two reviewers checking every data point and disagreements settled by consensus. A concrete look at chasing down a whole literature by rule rather than by impression.
  https://doi.org/10.1186/1741-7015-2-13
- **Blockchain Technology in Healthcare: A Systematic Review** _(high)_
  To survey blockchain use in healthcare, the authors followed a published step-by-step protocol (PRISMA), searching four databases with a pre-set search strategy to find, extract, and analyze every relevant study — a concrete example of a documented, repeatable search procedure rather than an ad-hoc reading.
  https://doi.org/10.3390/healthcare7020056
- **Clinical effectiveness of Invisalign® orthodontic treatment: a systematic review** _(high)_
  To map the evidence on a clear-aligner system, the authors followed a pre-set, repeatable procedure: searching multiple databases (including unpublished work), screening every hit independently and in duplicate with disagreements resolved by other authors, extracting data onto standard forms, and rating each study's risk of bias against fixed criteria — a concrete look at how an exhaustive, rule-governed evidence search is run.
  https://doi.org/10.1186/s40510-018-0235-z

**Considered but not accepted:**
- Application of systematic review methodology to food and feed safety assessments to support decision making — This is a guidance document about how to do systematic reviews; its subject matter is the systematic methodology itself, not a study that practiced being systematic in its own substantive inference. — https://doi.org/10.2903/j.efsa.2010.1637

## Conservative
*path:* Careful › Cautious

- **Global Estimate of Human Brucellosis Incidence** _(high)_
  To avoid overstating their case, the researchers deliberately left out factors (cases misdiagnosed as malaria or typhoid, and undiagnosed cases) that they knew would push their number higher, so their headline estimate is presented as a floor rather than a best guess — a concrete look at building a deliberately under-reaching conclusion.
  https://doi.org/10.3201/eid2909.230052
- **<i>Planck</i>2015 results** _(high)_
  Even though their polarization results passed an extensive battery of validation tests, the team deliberately downgraded those results to 'preliminary' because they knew of one unresolved mismatch between their simulated noise and the real data — choosing to underclaim rather than risk overstating.
  https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/201525836
- **The effectiveness of Schroth method in Cobb angle, quality of life and trunk rotation angle in adolescent idiopathic scoliosis: a systematic review and meta-analysis** _(medium)_
  Even after their pooled analysis showed a statistically significant benefit, the authors deliberately held back from calling it meaningful — they pointed out the spine-curve improvement fell short of the smallest change a patient would actually notice, and formally downgraded their own confidence in the evidence to 'low' and 'very low'.
  https://doi.org/10.23736/s1973-9087.23.07654-2

**Considered but not accepted:**
- Interpreting Posterior Relative Risk Estimates in Disease-Mapping Studies — The paper characterizes the conservatism (high specificity, low sensitivity) of disease-mapping models through simulation; conservatism is its object of study, not a cautious property of its own substantive inference. — https://doi.org/10.1289/ehp.6740
- Mathematical and Statistical Aspects of Estimating Small Oscillations Parameters in a Conservative Mechanical System Using Inaccurate Observations — The paper uses 'conservative' in the physics sense of an energy-conserving mechanical system, not the methodological caution meant by the target quality. — https://doi.org/10.3390/math11122643
- STATCONT: A statistical continuum level determination method for line-rich sources — This is a methods paper developing a continuum-determination tool; the single mention of a 'conservative' uncertainty value is a feature of the tool's output, not the researchers enacting cautious, conservative inference in their own substantive conclusion. — https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/201730425

## Measured
*path:* Humble › Cautious

- **An integrative review of the effects of high-intensity interval training on the autonomic nervous system** _(medium)_
  Having found mostly positive results, the authors deliberately hold back from cheerleading: they tally up why their evidence is shaky — wildly different training protocols, mostly male and small samples, an indirect heart-rate proxy, and the likelihood that null results went unpublished — and state plainly that their own appealing hypothesis 'does not demonstrate' the conclusion one might be tempted to draw.
  https://doi.org/10.1016/j.smhs.2024.08.002
- **Tyrosine kinase inhibitors as an alternative treatment in canine mast cell tumor** _(medium)_
  Despite finding that the targeted drugs beat standard chemotherapy on tumor-response rates, the authors deliberately hold back their conclusion — they flag that the pooled studies mixed dissimilar patients, that several were funded by the drug makers, and that the mutation tests were too crude to trust, and on that basis refuse to recommend the new drug as a first choice. A concrete example of letting acknowledged weaknesses rein in the headline claim.
  https://doi.org/10.3389/fvets.2023.1188795
- **The Effectiveness of Artificial Intelligence-Based Interventions for Students with Learning Disabilities: A Systematic Review** _(medium)_
  Even though all the studies they reviewed reported positive results, the authors formally graded how trustworthy each study was, found none were strong, and explicitly held back their own conclusion — calling for cautious interpretation rather than declaring the approach proven.
  https://doi.org/10.3390/brainsci15080806

**Considered but not accepted:**
- Commentary: Comparison of radiological interpretation made by veterinary radiologists and state-of-the-art commercial AI software for canine and feline radiographic studies — This is a critical commentary arguing that another study overstated its AI results and urging caution; it advocates for measured restraint rather than enacting a tempered inference in its own substantive research. — https://doi.org/10.3389/fvets.2025.1615947

## Representative
*path:* Fair › Inclusive

- **Epigenetic-based age acceleration in a representative sample of older Americans: Associations with aging-related morbidity and mortality** _(high)_
  The team built their findings on a nationally representative survey of older Americans and applied sample weights to correct for who actually got the blood test, so their conclusions speak for the broader older-US population rather than a convenience group — a concrete example of making a sample stand in for a whole population.
  https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/9992763
- **Generalized Trust and Intelligence in the United States** _(high)_
  To keep their sample mirroring the actual U.S. adult population, the authors weighted each interview to correct for people in larger households being less likely to be picked, and deliberately dropped years where one racial group had been over-sampled — a concrete look at the steps taken to make a sample stand in for a whole population.
  https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0091786
- **Recruitment of a Diverse Community-based Older Adult Cohort for a Longitudinal Aging Study** _(medium)_
  Setting out to fix a parent study that was 95% White, the team deliberately recruited within one majority-Black town and ended up with a cohort whose share of Black older adults (about 66%) matched their proportion in the surrounding community — a concrete case of building a sample that mirrors the population it is meant to speak for.
  https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/11178142

**Considered but not accepted:**
- Demographics of physics education research — The paper studies whether physics education research samples are representative — and finds they are not — so representativeness is its object of study, not a property its own method enacts. — https://doi.org/10.1103/physrevphyseducres.16.020106
- Representativeness of samples enrolled in Alzheimer's disease research centers — The paper's subject matter is representativeness itself — it measures and characterizes whether Alzheimer's research samples represent the U.S. population, rather than itself being a representative study practiced in service of its own substantive inference. — https://doi.org/10.1002/dad2.12450
- A Qualitative Study Exploring Barriers and Facilitators of Enrolling Underrepresented Populations in Clinical Trials and Biobanking — The paper's subject matter IS representation in trials—it studies barriers to enrolling underrepresented groups rather than its own research being a model of representative sampling (and it admits its sample was limited to English-speaking, single-state, mostly female participants). — https://doi.org/10.3389/fcell.2019.00074
- Inclusion of people of color in psychedelic-assisted psychotherapy: a review of the literature — The paper studies and measures whether OTHER studies' samples were representative of people of color; representativeness is its subject matter, not a property its own review enacts. — https://doi.org/10.1186/s12888-018-1824-6
- Barriers and recruitment strategies for precarious status migrants in Montreal, Canada — The paper's subject matter IS representation/inclusion in research — it analyzes and recommends recruitment strategies to increase representation of hard-to-reach migrants, rather than being a substantive study whose own conclusion is warranted by having a representative sample. — https://doi.org/10.1186/s12874-019-0683-2
- The ADNI4 Digital Study: A novel approach to recruitment, screening, and assessment of participants for AD clinical research — The paper's subject matter IS recruiting a representative/diverse sample — it evaluates the feasibility of a recruitment approach and even reports its shortfalls (low Latinx and low-education inclusion), so representativeness is the object of study, not an enacted property of a substantive inference. — https://doi.org/10.1002/alz.14234
- Understanding Barriers and Facilitators to Signing Up for a Mobile-Responsive Registry to Recruit Healthy Volunteers and Members of Underrepresented Communities for Alzheimer's Disease Prevention Studies — The paper's subject matter is recruiting representative, underrepresented groups into AD research; the study itself studies that topic and even admits its own sample was not a representative national sample, so it does not practice the quality. — https://doi.org/10.14283/jpad.2023.67
- Inclusive Recruitment Strategies to Maximize Sociodemographic Diversity among Participants: A St. Louis Case Study — The paper is a case study about inclusive recruitment methods, and it explicitly states its sample was intentionally NOT representative of the population, so it neither exhibits nor aims for representativeness. — https://doi.org/10.1177/23814683231183646
- Leveraging digital tools to enhance diversity and inclusion in clinical trial recruitment — This is a perspective/overview paper that discusses and recommends strategies for representative, diverse recruitment rather than reporting its own study that achieved a representative sample. — https://doi.org/10.3389/fpubh.2024.1483367
- Strategies for recruiting underrepresented in medicine and sexual and gender minority students to emergency medicine — The paper is about strategies for recruiting underrepresented groups—diversity/inclusion is its topic—and its own participant pool was a small convenience sample the authors themselves flag as non-representative, so the work discusses rather than enacts representativeness. — https://doi.org/10.1002/aet2.10873
- Enrollment of underrepresented racial and ethnic groups in the Rare and Atypical Diabetes Network (RADIANT) — The paper's subject matter IS representativeness in enrollment; it measures and reports that its sample was NOT representative (underrepresented groups fell below targets), so it studies the quality rather than exhibiting it. — https://doi.org/10.1017/cts.2022.529
- A Systematic Review on Participant Diversity in Clinical Trials—Have We Made Progress for the Management of Obesity and Its Metabolic Sequelae in Diet, Drug, and Surgical Trials — The paper studies and measures whether other trials' participant samples were representative; representativeness is its subject of study, not a property of its own method. — https://doi.org/10.1007/s40615-022-01487-0
- Using patient portals for large-scale recruitment of individuals underrepresented in biomedical research: an evaluation of engagement patterns throughout the patient portal recruitment process at a single site within the <i>All of Us Research Program</i> — The paper's subject matter IS representativeness in research recruitment—it evaluates engagement patterns of underrepresented groups rather than being a substantive study whose own sample was representative; it studies the quality rather than practicing it. — https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/11413441

## Representative
*path:* Reliable › Robust

- **Impact of diabetes mellitus on arterial stiffness in a representative sample of an urban Brazilian population** _(high)_
  To study a whole city's population rather than just clinic patients, the researchers randomly picked households across the city and then randomly selected one eligible resident per home, following an established population-survey protocol — a concrete example of building a sample meant to mirror the general population.
  https://doi.org/10.1186/1758-5996-5-45
- **Screening for loneliness in representative population samples: Validation of a single-item measure** _(high)_
  To draw their nearly 5,000 participants, the researchers had interviewers walk a randomized route through neighborhoods and used a fixed rule to pick which household member to interview, so the resulting group mirrored the national breakdown by age, sex, and education rather than whoever was easiest to reach.
  https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0279701
- **Prevalence of rearrangements in the 22q11.2 region and population-based risk of neuropsychiatric and developmental disorders in a Danish population: a case-cohort study** _(high)_
  The researchers built their estimates on a random 2% slice of the entire Danish population rather than a clinic-recruited group, and re-weighted the data by each person's known chance of being sampled so the prevalence and risk numbers reflect the whole population rather than a skewed subset — a concrete look at making a sample stand in for everyone.
  https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/6560180

**Considered but not accepted:**
- Defining representativeness of study samples in medical and population health research — The paper defines and characterizes the concept of representativeness itself; it is a methodological essay about the quality, not a study whose own sample was representative. — https://doi.org/10.1136/bmjmed-2022-000399
- Determinants of Self-Rated Health in a Representative Sample of a Rural Population: A Cross-Sectional Study in Greece — The abstract merely asserts the sample is 'representative of the rural population' without showing any sampling design or evidence that demonstrates representativeness. — https://doi.org/10.3390/ijerph9030943
- External Validity: From Do-Calculus to Transportability Across Populations — This is a theoretical/methodological paper that develops a formal framework for generalizing causal effects across populations; it studies external validity rather than being a substantive study that itself used a representative sample. — http://arxiv.org/abs/1503.01603
- Achieving external validity in home advantage research: generalizing crowd noise effects — This is a focused review whose subject matter is external validity and representative design itself; it discusses and argues for representativeness rather than the article being a substantive study that enacted a representative sample to warrant its own conclusion. — https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2014.00532
- Generalizability of cognitive results from clinical trial participants to an older adult population: Addressing external validity — The paper's subject matter is generalizability/representativeness itself — it develops and demonstrates a weighting method to address external validity, and even finds its own trial sample was NOT representative; it studies the quality rather than its own study being representative. — https://doi.org/10.1002/dad2.12417
- No generalized transverse momentum dependent factorization in the hadroproduction of high transverse momentum hadrons — Theoretical particle-physics paper on factorization; does not engage 'Representative' (e.g. a sample representing a population) in any way. — http://arxiv.org/abs/1001.2977
- When all children comprehend: increasing the external validity of narrative comprehension development research — This is a review arguing for more externally valid, representative-sample research; it discusses and advocates representativeness rather than conducting its own study on a representative sample. — https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2014.00168

## Consenting
*path:* Fair › Respectful

_(no instances accepted)_

**Considered but not accepted:**
- Taking part in a pharmacogenetic clinical trial: assessment of trial participants understanding of information disclosed during the informed consent process — The paper's subject matter IS the informed consent process — it assesses participants' understanding of consent rather than the study itself being an exemplary instance of consenting. — https://doi.org/10.1186/1472-6939-14-34
- Informed consent and ethics committee approval in laboratory medicine — This is a guidance article ABOUT informed consent and ethics approval in laboratory medicine; it discusses the quality rather than being a study that itself obtained consent for its own substantive research. — https://doi.org/10.11613/bm.2018.030201
- Knowledge and Practices of Obtaining Informed Consent for Medical Procedures among Specialist Physicians: Questionnaire Study in 6 Croatian Hospitals — The paper's subject matter IS informed consent — it surveys physicians' knowledge and practices of obtaining consent; it studies the quality rather than the study itself enacting it on its own research participants. — https://doi.org/10.3325/cmj.2009.50.567
- Revisiting informed consent in forensic genomics in light of current technologies and the times — The paper is a review/argument ABOUT informed consent practices in forensic genomics; it studies and recommends consent rather than being a study that itself obtained consent for its own substantive inquiry. — https://doi.org/10.1007/s00414-023-02947-w
- Adequacy of Informed Consent in Elective Surgical Procedures: A Study in a Navi Mumbai Tertiary Care Centre — The paper studies and audits the adequacy of informed consent in others' surgical practice; consent is its subject matter, not a method warranting its own substantive inference. — https://doi.org/10.7759/cureus.41777
- Practice variation across consent templates for biobank research. a survey of German biobanks — The paper studies and compares others' consent forms as its subject matter rather than the study itself enacting respectful consent in its own conduct. — https://doi.org/10.3389/fgene.2013.00240
- Comprehension of informed consent and voluntary participation in registration cohorts for phase IIb HIV vaccine trial in Dar Es Salaam, Tanzania: a qualitative descriptive study — The paper studies and characterizes participants' comprehension of informed consent in HIV trials—the quality is its subject matter, not a property enacted in service of its own substantive inference. — https://doi.org/10.1186/s12910-024-01033-z
- An evaluation of the process of informed consent: views from research participants and staff — The paper studies the informed consent process itself via surveys rather than enacting consent as the method of its own substantive research. — https://doi.org/10.1186/s13063-021-05493-1
- Empty ethics: the problem with informed consent — The paper studies and critiques informed consent as its subject matter rather than the researchers themselves practicing consent in a way that warrants their own substantive inference. — https://doi.org/10.1046/j.1467-9566.2003.00369.x
- Improving understanding in the research informed consent process: a systematic review of 54 interventions tested in randomized control trials — The paper reviews and studies informed-consent interventions as its subject matter rather than itself being a study that practiced consent in service of its own substantive inference. — https://doi.org/10.1186/1472-6939-14-28
- Incorporating a quiz into informed consent processes: Qualitative study of participants' reactions — The paper's subject matter IS the informed-consent process — it studies participants' reactions to a consent comprehension quiz rather than enacting consent in service of its own substantive inquiry. — https://doi.org/10.1186/1475-2875-6-145
- Self-directed multimedia process for delivering participant informed consent — The paper's subject matter is the informed-consent process itself — it compares ways of obtaining consent — so it studies the quality rather than merely practicing it as a property of an unrelated study. — https://doi.org/10.1136/bmjopen-2020-036977
- The reality of informed consent: empirical studies on patient comprehension—systematic review — This is a systematic review studying patients' comprehension of informed consent; it makes the quality its object of study rather than practicing genuine consent in its own substantive research. — https://doi.org/10.1186/s13063-020-04969-w
- Audio-visual presentation of information for informed consent for participation in clinical trials — This is a systematic review studying methods of informed consent in other trials — consent is its subject matter, not a quality its own research practiced. — https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.cd003717.pub3
- Informed consent and participant perceptions of influenza vaccine trials in South Africa — The paper studies and evaluates the informed-consent process in others, making consent its object of study rather than a quality its own conduct enacts. — https://doi.org/10.1136/jme.2004.009910
- A Modern History of Informed Consent and the Role of Key Information — This is a review of the history and regulation of informed consent; it studies the quality rather than the study itself enacting consent in its own substantive research. — https://doi.org/10.31486/toj.19.0105
- Informed consent, parental awareness, and reasons for participating in a randomised controlled study — The paper studies and evaluates the informed-consent process itself as its subject matter, rather than being a study that simply obtained proper consent in service of some other inquiry. — https://doi.org/10.1136/adc.79.2.120
- Tailoring the process of informed consent in genetic and genomic research — The paper discusses and recommends how to tailor informed consent in genomic research rather than being a study that itself obtained consent from its own participants. — https://doi.org/10.1186/gm141
- Researchers’ views on, and experiences with, the requirement to obtain informed consent in research involving human participants: a qualitative study — The paper studies researchers' views and experiences with informed consent rather than the study itself enacting consent of its own participants. — https://doi.org/10.1186/s12910-020-00538-7
- Ten years of dynamic consent in the CHRIS study: informed consent as a dynamic process — The paper's subject matter IS the consent model itself — it describes, evaluates, and reflects on the CHRIS study's dynamic consent process rather than being a substantive study whose finding is warranted by having obtained consent. — https://doi.org/10.1038/s41431-022-01160-4

## Protective
*path:* Fair › Respectful

- **Safeguarding in adolescent mental health research: navigating dilemmas and developing procedures** _(medium)_
  When the team found that a quarter of the 12–15-year-olds in their study reported recent thoughts of self-harm, they didn't just note it — they built and ran real protective machinery: same-day encrypted alerts to each school's safeguarding lead, required read-receipts, no data collection on Fridays so weekend risks wouldn't go unaddressed, and consultation with young people who'd lived through mental ill health. A concrete look at protecting vulnerable participants in practice.
  https://doi.org/10.1136/bmjopen-2023-076700
- **Human rights abuses and collective resilience among sex workers in four African countries: a qualitative study** _(medium)_
  To shield an extremely vulnerable, criminalized group, the researchers held interviews only in places where safety and privacy could be maximized, kept real names solely on consent forms and replaced them with codes everywhere else, and referred any participant who needed it to local counselling and legal help — a concrete picture of building safeguards into a study of people at real risk.
  https://doi.org/10.1186/1744-8603-9-33
- **Towards cross-Canada monitoring of the unregulated street drug supply** _(medium)_
  Working with a criminalized, stigmatized population, the researchers built deliberate safeguards into the study itself: people took part anonymously with only verbal consent and no identifying information, their survey and urine sample were linked by an anonymous code, and the data are deliberately withheld from public release to keep participants from being exposed — a concrete look at designing research to shield vulnerable people from harm.
  https://doi.org/10.1186/s12889-021-11757-x

- A Critical Examination of Child Protection Initiatives in Sport Contexts — The paper studies and critiques child protection initiatives as its subject matter rather than the research itself being protective of anyone. — https://doi.org/10.3390/socsci3040742

- Green Lights and Red Flags: The (Im)Possibilities of Contextual Safeguarding Responses to Extra-Familial Harm in the UK — The paper studies child-protection/safeguarding systems as its subject matter rather than the research itself enacting a protective quality. — https://doi.org/10.3390/socsci11070303

- Reducing the Harms of Nonclinical Psychedelics Use Through a Peer-Support Telephone Helpline — The protection of people from harm is the subject matter being studied (a harm-reduction helpline), not a protective quality the research itself enacted toward its own participants or inference. — https://doi.org/10.1089/psymed.2022.0017

## Jargon-free
*path:* Clear › Legible

- **Semaglutide treatment for obesity in teenagers: a plain language summary of the STEP TEENS research study** _(high)_
  This is a plain-language retelling of a clinical trial that swaps every technical term for an everyday one as it goes — calling a placebo a 'dummy medicine' and spelling out 'body mass index' — a concrete model of how to strip jargon out of dense medical findings.
  https://doi.org/10.2217/cer-2022-0187
- **Plain language summary of 2022 cancer statistics: Focus on lung cancer** _(medium)_
  The whole document is a deliberate plain-language rewrite of a technical cancer-statistics article, swapping clinical terms for everyday phrasing — turning a forecast of diagnoses and deaths into sentences any reader can follow. A concrete model of stripping jargon out of dense numerical findings.
  https://doi.org/10.2217/fon-2022-1214
- **The amyloid-β Pathway in Alzheimer’s Disease: A Plain Language Summary** _(medium)_
  This is a deliberately written plain-language version of a technical Alzheimer's review, where each specialist term is unpacked on the spot — for instance, calling amyloid-β 'a protein fragment (or peptide)' rather than leaving the word unexplained. A concrete look at rewriting dense science so a non-specialist can follow it.
  https://doi.org/10.2217/nmt-2022-0037
